chapter: Cafe Society and the Zodiac Suite
title: Moe Asch's love of artists, and bringing Erroll Garner and Art Tatum to him
summary: Asch let artists record whatever they wanted. She brought in Erroll Garner and Art Tatum, who recorded for little money, and she took Asch's recordings to Pittsburgh.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Recording for Moe Asch, was that different from recording for other people?

Yes, it was different because Moe Ash had more love and he had more respect for jazz artists. Often he would take us to dinner, the nicest dinners, steak dinners, the nicest places and it was his idea that an artist should be heard if they're talented. He'd turn the tape on and go away, let you record anything you wanted to record and it always worked out great. He wanted to record Erroll Garner, you know. Erroll Garner was in Pittsburgh. I went there

on a vacation. By the way, we're both from Pittsburgh. He had been to New York and was a little discouraged. I said, "Come on back." So he came back later on, his girl friend or someone brought him here. Moe Ash heard Erroll Garner and he said, "Mary, try to get Errd1 Garner and Art Tatum to record." I knew Errd1 Garner needed money. I said, "I think it will cost you about $1500 for Art Tatum; $750 for Errd1." He said, "I don't care; I'll pay them. Get them." Moe Ash was so great that when I talked with Art Tatum, Art Tatum charged him $750. I said, "Why, he was willing to pay you more money?" He said, "As great as that man is, I record for him for nothing." Erroll Garner asked him for $250. That's how great he is. I guess that's the reason why he has no money. Like, Victor sued him once and he said he didn't care because he was going to put the records out because he had sold them some tapes and they didn't put the tapes out. He said, "Because a real artist should be heard." At one time he had all the great records, like of Indians and something unusual and folk singers and everything, and the major companies had to buy the tapes from him. Because if you're talented he doesn't bother you about what you should do and whatnot. He'd just tell you to go ahead and record what you wanted to record.
But after you made the records for Moe did they get out much? Was there much circulation?

Yes, they did, they got out quite a bit. He did business with somebody else. I forget the name of that company. He did all kinds of things trying to get the artists heard. That was his main thing. I've done recordings with Josh White and a lot of artists there. I'd get a lot of recording artists for him and then he allowed me to go to Pittsburgh to record some musicians. I went there.
